finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but ignores the returned boolean. Any authenticated user can run purgeAll(), which is meant to be admin-only. rotateKeys uses mustPerm correctly, which shows the intended pattern.
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user sending a request to the purge endpoint
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) gets the current user from the request context
checkPerm returns false for non-admins, but the result is discarded and no 403 is written

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm only returns a bool and does not write an error response. mustPerm is not used in purge. This is the only Go file in the repo, so there is no middleware or router code that could enforce admin access. If the real app has such middleware outside this repo, it was not visible to this audit.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 returns a bool that is discarded at line 26; no middleware or router exists in the repo, which has only handlers.go)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement and discards the bool, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 which tests mustPerm's result.
